title: Celestial Axis Inference — Directional Statistics, Frames, Precession and Toroidal Geometry
status: astronomical directional-statistics framework + project-claim audit; symbolic meanings remain separate
abstract: Celestial-axis claims become scientific only after the axis, reference frame, epoch, target set and uncertainty are explicitly defined. This redevelopment extends the existing coordinate machinery into a directional-statistics theory. Named objects are mapped to unit vectors in a common astrometric frame; a candidate axis is estimated from a preregistered target set; angular residuals are propagated through positional and frame uncertainties; and alignment is compared against isotropic or survey-conditioned nulls with search multiplicity included. This changes the question from 'do these stars seem to line up with North?' to 'what axis best explains the declared target directions, how uncertain is it, and is its concentration stronger than expected under a null chosen before inspection?' The framework also keeps geographic, equatorial, galactic, geomagnetic and local-horizon coordinates explicitly distinct. Precession/proper motion are transformations, not numerological coincidences. The torus branch is likewise formalized as an inverse-geometry problem: one circumference cannot determine both major and minor radii. The result is a reproducible measurement programme that can test physical directional claims while preserving symbolic North/Sirius/Regulus motifs as a separate interpretive layer.
research_question: Given a preregistered set of celestial targets, is there a statistically identifiable axis that explains their directions better than isotropic or survey-conditioned null models, and is that axis stable across epoch/frame transformations and uncertainty propagation?
measurement_contract: Declare coordinate system, frame and epoch.
Define whether the axis is directed or undirected.
Correct for searched stars/axes/epochs/tolerances where applicable.
Report physical result separately from symbolic interpretation.

vector_geometry.equatorial: n(alpha,delta)=(cos delta cos alpha, cos delta sin alpha, sin delta)
vector_geometry.unit_rule: alpha,delta are radians in trigonometric calculations; n and a are unit vectors.

axis_estimation.quadratic_objective: maximize a^T M a subject to a^T a=1, with M=sum_i w_i n_i n_i^T
axis_estimation.solution: dominant eigenvector of M for an undirected quadratic-concentration axis
axis_estimation.interpretation: The axis is inferred from the declared data rather than drawn after inspection.

directional_probability.fisher_distribution: p(n|mu,kappa)=C(kappa) exp(kappa mu dot n) for a directed spherical concentration model
directional_probability.watson_neighbor: For undirected axial data, use an axial distribution such as Watson/Bingham rather than duplicating +a and -a informally.
directional_probability.null: kappa=0 corresponds to isotropy for the Fisher model.
directional_probability.test: Estimate concentration with uncertainty and compare against isotropic/survey-conditioned simulations.

null_and_multiple_testing.single_cap: For an isotropic directed target, P(psi<=psi0)=(1-cos psi0)/2.
null_and_multiple_testing.undirected_cap: For either pole of an undirected axis and psi0<=pi/2, P=1-cos psi0.
null_and_multiple_testing.look_elsewhere: If many targets, coordinate frames, dates, symbolic correspondences or tolerances were explored, simulate the complete search procedure under the null and compare the best-found statistic, not only the final nominal angle.
null_and_multiple_testing.survey_null: When target discovery/catalog selection is nonuniform, random directions should be drawn from the effective selection function rather than an ideal isotropic sky.

uncertainty.frame: Apply validated astrometric transformations for precession/nutation/Earth orientation.
uncertainty.axis: Refit the axis in each Monte Carlo draw to obtain p(a|data) or an empirical confidence region.
uncertainty.report: Quote angular residual distributions and axis uncertainty rather than a single over-precise bearing.

local_horizon.altitude: sin h=sin phi sin delta+cos phi cos delta cos H
local_horizon.meaning: A local pointing claim depends on observer latitude/longitude and time; it cannot be tested with RA/Dec alone.

epoch_dynamics.precession_rate: Omega_p=2 pi/T_p is an angular frequency, not a length or Galactic distance.
epoch_dynamics.stability_test: Track psi_i(t) or inferred axis a(t) across the historical epoch range if the claim is explicitly temporal.

worked_project_sanity_check.sirius_regulus: Using J2000 ICRS catalog positions gives an angular separation near 57.8 degrees; neither is collinear with the north celestial pole in this coordinate sense.
worked_project_sanity_check.interpretation: The physical result constrains astronomical-axis claims but says nothing about whether Dog/Lion/North symbolism is meaningful within the project.

torus_inverse_problem.geometry: A=4 pi^2 Rr; V=2 pi^2 Rr^2; C_major=2 pi R; C_minor=2 pi r
torus_inverse_problem.identifiability: One scalar circumference-like measurement supplies at most one independent constraint on two unknown radii R and r.
torus_inverse_problem.posterior: p(R,r|d) proportional to p(d|R,r)p(R,r) if uncertain historical measurement and priors are available.
torus_inverse_problem.rule: Do not infer area, volume or aspect ratio from one recovered length without another independent constraint.

failure_conditions: Alignment significance disappears after reproducing the full look-elsewhere/search procedure under the null.
The inferred axis changes substantially under reasonable target definitions, epochs or uncertainty propagation.
A claimed local-horizon alignment cannot be reproduced for the stated observer/time.
Different coordinate systems are compared without a valid transformation.
A torus geometry is claimed from fewer independent measurements than unknown geometric parameters.
next_decisive_work: Choose one historical/public celestial-axis claim and freeze its target set before fitting.
Run the directional-statistics pipeline with epoch-corrected catalog uncertainties.
Simulate the complete selection/search process to obtain an experiment-level null probability.
Only after a robust physical result compare it with the symbolic chronology as a separate interpretive question.
